what_happened: Direct read of orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh shows the postflight extension-hook stage can never fire for ANY extension dispatched via /orchestrate's own cycle: skill_postflight_update's internal skill_run_extension_hook call reads an ambient ${TASK_TYPE:-} global that this script never sets (only a lowercase local task_type exists, from its own --task-type CLI flag). This blocks both the producing (plan) and consuming (--check, implement) call sites this task needs, and is a generic core bug, not lean-specific. A precedented fix exists: command-gate-out.sh already resolves task_type locally and passes it directly to skill_run_extension_hook for the verification stage.

Idempotence/immutability hard constraint resolved for free: lean-challenge-snapshot.sh already refuses (exit 73) to overwrite an existing manifest without --force, independent of the status gate. A postflight hook invoking the script plainly inherits 'refuse' as the re-plan behaviour with zero new code. Both inertness hard constraints (non-lean task type; zero-goal lean4 plan) are likewise already satisfied by landed mechanisms (skill_get_extension_dir's task_type match, and task 385's zero-goal marker/exit-72 handling) requiring no new hook-side logic.

Plan-time re-derivation found a landed seam the research report never considered: the post-task OBSERVER seam (manifest 'observers' object -> run-task-observers.sh), invoked unconditionally from orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's completion path with the correctly-resolved LOCAL task_type and the fresh persisted_status. It sidesteps the report's entire premise that a core TASK_TYPE bridging fix is a prerequisite: the observer path has no such bug, is advisory/non-blocking by explicit contract, and needs ZERO core edits. A live precedent exists (books extension's books-observe.sh + tests/test-books-observe.sh). Registration option (c) therefore supersedes the dispatch's (a)/(b) and the report's recommendation.

Research report asserted the postflight lifecycle hook receives an empty TASK_DIR as well as an empty TASK_TYPE from orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh. Re-derivation shows TASK_DIR IS set (uppercase global, lines 439-440); only TASK_TYPE is absent. Separately, core's own docs/guides/creating-extensions.md lines 937-942 already document the TASK_TYPE gap AND carry a directive not to 'fix' it by plumbing TASK_TYPE through the postflight hook -- a directive the report's primary recommendation would have violated.

Phase 2's verify-touched.sh agent-system/extensions/lean/manifest.json run (36 suites) reported 2 failing suites under heavy concurrent sibling batch load: test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh (TIMEOUT, already tagged EXPECTED by run-all.sh) and test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh case(q) (a wall-clock timing comparison, tagged NEW). Re-ran test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh in isolation: 29/29 passed, confirming the failure was concurrent-load timing flakiness, not a regression from the observers block or provides.scripts additions to the lean manifest.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/lean/README.md' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.

Phase 3's new re-plan regression pins (M4/M5) surfaced a precise fact worth recording in Phase 4's design doc: lean-challenge-snapshot.sh's loud INCIDENT warning is printed ONLY when --force bypasses the STATUS gate (past-planned); a plain re-plan overwrite with --force while status is still 'planned' (bypassing only the manifest-exists refusal) is silent -- rc 0, manifest overwritten, no warning text. The plan's own phrasing ('the same invocation with --force overwrites it and warns') is imprecise for this specific sub-case; Phase 4's design-record edit should state the warning's actual scope precisely.

Phase 5's full in-dispatch verify-touched.sh run (40 suites, OWED free-class fallback) reported test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh as a TIMEOUT failure (exceeded the 600s per-suite bound), tagged EXPECTED by run-all.sh. Re-ran it standalone: 17/17 passed cleanly. This is the same class of concurrent-sibling-load timing flakiness already recorded in this task's Phase 2 issue log entry, confirmed unrelated to any file this task touches (test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh exercises verify-deploy.sh's gate-caching mechanism, not the lean Challenge observer). All lean-specific suites (test-lean-challenge-observe.sh, test-lean-challenge-snapshot.sh) passed in the same batch run.
